content.value: Horses begin at level 1 and cap at 30. Each level after 1 grants +10 maximum HP, +0.5% base speed, +0.35% base jump, +2 evasion, and +1.5 maximum stamina.

Normal ridden travel: 2 XP for every accumulated 10 horizontal blocks.
Galloping travel: 4 XP for every accumulated 10 horizontal blocks.
Perfect ridden jump: 3 XP when the horse leaves the ground upward.
Long jump: +2 XP at four horizontal blocks, then +2 per additional two blocks, capped at +10 at twelve blocks.
Mounted kill: XP equal to the defeated target's maximum health, rounded and clamped between 5 and 50.

Hold Sprint and Forward while riding to gallop. Ordinary movement does not use stamina. Gallop begins with +15% total horse speed and consumes 4 stamina per second. Level 30 adds another +5% gallop speed, Swift adds +5%, and road surfaces add a separate +10%. Mobility bonuses stop increasing at the horse's movement-speed cap.

At zero stamina the horse becomes exhausted and cannot gallop. Ordinary movement and perfect jumps remain available. Exhaustion ends at 20% stamina, so continuing to hold Sprint automatically resumes gallop after sufficient recovery.

Maximum stamina is genetic Endurance + 1.5 per trained level after level 1, then Hardy's bonus if present. A jump normally costs 8 stamina. Stamina starts recovering two seconds after the last gallop or jump: 2 per second while mounted and 4 per second while unmounted. Recovery pauses while the horse is airborne.
Stamina never prevents jumping. At zero stamina, pressing Jump still performs that horse's full genetic jump; only Gallop is locked.

Level 5 — Trail Training: +20% terrain movement efficiency.
Level 10 — Second Wind: +0.5 mounted stamina recovery per second.
Level 15 — Efficient Jumper: jump cost falls from 8 to 6.
Level 20 — Sure Stride: +0.25 step height, +2 safe-fall distance, 20% less remaining fall damage, and improved water movement.
Level 25 — Endurance Training: gallop cost falls from 4 to 3 per second.
Level 30 — Mastered Gallop: +5% gallop speed.

Horse jumps have no charge timing. Pressing Jump immediately performs a full-strength jump, and the normal player XP bar stays visible instead of the vanilla mount-charge bar. The actual height still depends on the horse's Jump gene, training, imprint, and trait.

Ridden horses preserve their horizontal momentum throughout jumps and terrain-following ledge drops while the rider continues moving. Small drops pull the horse toward the nearby surface instead of launching it into a long glide, so descending rough terrain remains controlled. Releasing Forward, colliding with a wall, moving backward, or entering water allows the horse to slow normally.
Recognized roads give horses +10% speed. Paths, gravel, packed mud, stone and brick, planks, slabs, and stairs count as roads.
The mounted stamina HUD can be moved and scaled in Mod Menu's HUD Layout screen. It displays Gallop or Recovering when those states are active.
